about: Topic map of the AP Calculus AB part of the AP Calculus AB and BC Course and Exam Description, written in LevlPrep's own words from docs/apcalc-research/framework.md. No CED text is reproduced. Units 1-2 objectives and the epsilon-delta exclusion were read in the CED; Units 3-8 summaries come from knowledge of the CED and must be verified (docs/apcalc-needs-author.md, units3to8-objectives). BC-only topics are listed as excluded.

ced.title: AP Calculus AB and BC Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: 2019 framework, reissued effective fall 2020 (content unchanged since)
ced.effective: Fall 2020; May 2027 MCQ timing per the fall 2026 clarifications
ced.verification: CED PDF text read through the Unit 3 opener; topic names for Units 3-8 from the partial extraction plus a third-party CED alignment list.

skillNames.1.A: Identify the question to be answered (not assessed)
skillNames.1.C: Choose a rule or procedure from the form of an expression
skillNames.1.D: Choose a rule or procedure from relationships between concepts
skillNames.1.E: Apply rules or procedures, with and without technology
skillNames.1.F: Explain how an approximation relates to the actual value

skillNames.2.B: Read information from graphs, tables, formulas and words
skillNames.2.D: Relate properties of a function across representations
skillNames.2.E: Relate representations of a function and its derivatives

skillNames.3.A: Use technology to form conjectures (not assessed)
skillNames.3.B: Pick the right definition, theorem or test
skillNames.3.E: Give reasons for solutions and conclusions
skillNames.3.G: Confirm a solution is accurate and appropriate

mathematicalPracticesNote: Weights from the current course page (verbatim ranges). Practice 4 (Communication and Notation) is not assessed in multiple choice, so it is free response only here; skills 1.A, 1.B and 3.A are not assessed.

topics.title: Can Change Happen at an Instant?
objectives: Explain why a rate at one instant has to be found as a limit of average rates.
knowledge: An average rate of change is measured over an interval; over an interval of length zero it is undefined.
Shrinking the interval and watching the average rates settle is what calculus calls a limit.

topics.title: What a Limit Is and How to Write It
objectives: Write and read limit notation.
knowledge: The limit of f(x) as x approaches c is the value f(x) gets close to as x gets close to c, whatever happens at c itself.
A limit can be shown with a graph, a table or a formula.
exclusions: The epsilon-delta definition of a limit is not assessed.

topics.title: Reading Limits from a Graph
objectives: Estimate limits, including one-sided limits, from a graph.
knowledge: A two-sided limit exists only when the left and right limits exist and are equal.
A limit can fail to exist because of a jump, unbounded growth or oscillation.
A graph drawn at the wrong scale can hide what a function does near a point.

topics.title: Estimating Limits from Tables
objectives: Estimate a limit from a table of values.
knowledge: Read the outputs as the inputs close in from both sides; agreement suggests the limit.

topics.title: Limit Laws
objectives: Find limits with the algebraic properties of limits.
knowledge: Limits of sums, differences, products, quotients (nonzero denominator) and compositions follow from the limits of the parts.

topics.title: Limits by Algebra: Factor, Rationalize, Simplify
objectives: Rewrite an expression into an equivalent form to find a limit.
knowledge: When substitution gives 0/0, factor, rationalize or simplify first, then substitute.

topics.title: Choosing a Way to Find a Limit
objectives: Pick a procedure for a limit from the form of the expression.
knowledge: Try substitution first; the form of the result tells you what to do next.

topics.title: The Squeeze Theorem
objectives: Find a limit with the squeeze theorem.
knowledge: If g(x) <= f(x) <= h(x) near c and g and h have the same limit L at c, then f has limit L there too.

topics.title: Limits Across Graphs, Tables and Formulas
objectives: Connect a limit across graphs, tables and formulas.
knowledge: The same limit can be read from each representation; move between them to answer a question.

topics.title: Types of Discontinuity
objectives: Name the kind of discontinuity a function has.
knowledge: Removable discontinuities, jump discontinuities and discontinuities from vertical asymptotes are the three kinds.

topics.title: Continuity at a Point
objectives: Decide whether a function is continuous at a point, with the definition.
knowledge: f is continuous at c when f(c) is defined, the limit at c exists, and the two are equal.

topics.title: Continuity on an Interval
objectives: Decide where a function is continuous.
knowledge: Continuous on an interval means continuous at every point of it.
Polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions are continuous on their domains.

topics.title: Removing a Discontinuity
objectives: Choose a value or a parameter that makes a function continuous.
knowledge: A removable discontinuity is removed by defining the function at the point to equal its limit.
At a break in a piecewise function, both pieces and the value must agree.

topics.title: Infinite Limits and Vertical Asymptotes
objectives: Describe a vertical asymptote with limits.
knowledge: An infinite limit says the function grows without bound; it is a way of saying the limit does not exist.

topics.title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
objectives: Find limits at infinity and describe end behavior.
knowledge: A finite limit at infinity gives a horizontal asymptote.
Comparing how fast functions grow tells which term dominates.

topics.title: The Intermediate Value Theorem
objectives: Justify that a value is reached with the Intermediate Value Theorem.
knowledge: If f is continuous on [a, b] and d is between f(a) and f(b), some c in (a, b) has f(c) = d.
A justification states continuity on the closed interval and the value being between.

topics.title: Average and Instantaneous Rates of Change
objectives: Find average rates of change and describe an instantaneous rate as a limit of difference quotients.
knowledge: The average rate of change on [a, b] is (f(b) - f(a))/(b - a), the slope of the secant line.

topics.title: The Derivative and Its Notation
objectives: Define the derivative, use its notations and write a tangent line.
knowledge: The derivative f'(a) is the limit of the difference quotient as h approaches 0.
Notations: f'(x), dy/dx, y'.
The derivative at a point is the slope of the tangent line there.

topics.title: Estimating a Derivative at a Point
objectives: Estimate a derivative from a graph or a table.
knowledge: Use the values on both sides of the point; technology can also estimate a derivative.

topics.title: Differentiability and Continuity
objectives: Explain where a function is or is not differentiable.
knowledge: Differentiable implies continuous; continuous does not imply differentiable.
Corners, cusps, vertical tangents and discontinuities are where derivatives fail to exist.

topics.title: The Power Rule
objectives: Differentiate powers of x.
knowledge: The derivative of x to the n is n times x to the n - 1, for any real n.

topics.title: Constant, Sum, Difference and Constant Multiple Rules
objectives: Differentiate sums, differences and constant multiples; differentiate polynomials.
knowledge: The derivative of a constant is 0; derivatives pass through sums and constant factors.

topics.title: Derivatives of sin x, cos x, e to the x and ln x
objectives: Differentiate the four basic transcendental functions and recognize a limit as a derivative.
knowledge: sin becomes cos, cos becomes -sin, e to the x is its own derivative, ln x becomes 1/x.
Some limits of difference quotients are a known derivative in disguise.

topics.title: The Product Rule
objectives: Differentiate a product.
knowledge: (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

topics.title: The Quotient Rule
objectives: Differentiate a quotient.
knowledge: (f/g)' = (f'g - fg')/g squared, where g is not 0.

topics.title: Derivatives of tan, cot, sec and csc
objectives: Differentiate the other four trigonometric functions.
knowledge: Rewrite each with sine and cosine and use the quotient rule.

units.title: Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions

topics.title: The Chain Rule
objectives: Differentiate a composite function.
knowledge: The derivative of f(g(x)) is f'(g(x)) times g'(x).

topics.title: Implicit Differentiation
objectives: Find dy/dx from an equation that relates x and y.
knowledge: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, using the chain rule on every y term; dy/dx may depend on x and y.

topics.title: Derivatives of Inverse Functions
objectives: Find the derivative of an inverse function at a point.
knowledge: If g is the inverse of f, g'(a) = 1/f'(g(a)); tables and graphs of f are enough.

topics.title: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Differentiate inverse trigonometric functions.
knowledge: arcsin, arccos and arctan have derivatives built from 1 - x squared and 1 + x squared.

topics.title: Choosing a Differentiation Rule
objectives: Choose and combine derivative rules for an expression.
knowledge: The outermost operation decides the first rule to use.

topics.title: Second and Higher Derivatives
objectives: Find second and higher derivatives, including of implicit relations.
knowledge: f'' is the derivative of f'; notations f''(x), d2y/dx2, y''.

topics.title: The Derivative in Context
objectives: Interpret a derivative in context, with units.
knowledge: A derivative has units of output per unit of input.

topics.title: Straight-Line Motion: Position, Velocity, Acceleration
objectives: Relate position, velocity and acceleration of a particle on a line.
knowledge: Speed is the absolute value of velocity; a particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign.

topics.title: Rates of Change in Other Contexts
objectives: Interpret rates of change outside motion.
knowledge: Population, temperature, volume and cost all have rates read the same way.

topics.title: Introduction to Related Rates
objectives: Differentiate a relation between quantities with respect to time.
knowledge: Every quantity that changes is a function of t; the chain rule links their rates.

topics.title: Solving Related Rates Problems
objectives: Solve and interpret related rates problems.
knowledge: Differentiate first, then substitute the values at the instant asked about.

topics.title: Local Linearity and Linearization
objectives: Estimate values with the tangent line and say whether the estimate is over or under.
knowledge: Near a point, a differentiable function is close to its tangent line.
The sign of the second derivative tells whether the tangent line is above or below the curve.

topics.title: L'Hospital's Rule
objectives: Find limits of 0/0 and infinity/infinity forms with L'Hospital's rule.
knowledge: Show both limits are 0 (or both infinite) before using the rule.

topics.title: The Mean Value Theorem
objectives: Justify a conclusion with the Mean Value Theorem.
knowledge: If f is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), some c in (a, b) has f'(c) equal to the average rate of change.

topics.title: Extreme Value Theorem, Global and Local Extrema, Critical Points
objectives: Use the Extreme Value Theorem and find critical points.
knowledge: A function continuous on [a, b] has at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value there.
A critical point is an interior point where f' is 0 or undefined.

topics.title: Where a Function Increases or Decreases
objectives: Find intervals of increase and decrease from the derivative.
knowledge: f is increasing where f' > 0 and decreasing where f' < 0.

topics.title: The First Derivative Test
objectives: Find relative extrema with the first derivative test.
knowledge: A relative extremum needs f' to change sign, not just to equal 0.

topics.title: The Candidates Test
objectives: Find absolute extrema on a closed interval.
knowledge: Compare f at every critical point and both endpoints.

topics.title: Concavity and Points of Inflection
objectives: Find intervals of concavity and points of inflection.
knowledge: Concave up where f' increases (f'' > 0), down where f' decreases (f'' < 0); an inflection point needs a change of concavity.

topics.title: The Second Derivative Test
objectives: Classify critical points with the second derivative.
knowledge: f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) > 0 gives a relative minimum; f''(c) < 0 a relative maximum.
A continuous function with exactly one critical point on an interval, a relative extremum, has its absolute extremum there.

topics.title: Sketching f, f' and f''
objectives: Sketch a function or its derivatives from one another.
knowledge: Key features of f come from the signs of f' and f''.

topics.title: Connecting f, f' and f''
objectives: Connect features of f, f' and f'' in any representation.
knowledge: A graph of f' is read for where f increases, has extrema and changes concavity.

topics.title: Introduction to Optimization
objectives: Set up an optimization problem in context.
knowledge: Write the quantity to optimize as a function of one variable on an interval.

topics.title: Solving Optimization Problems
objectives: Solve an optimization problem and justify the absolute extremum.
knowledge: Find critical points, then justify the absolute extremum with the candidates test or a global argument.

topics.title: Behavior of Implicit Relations
objectives: Find horizontal and vertical tangents and extrema of implicit relations.
knowledge: Horizontal tangent: the numerator of dy/dx is 0 and the denominator is not, at a point on the curve.
Vertical tangent: the denominator is 0 and the numerator is not.

topics.title: Accumulating Change
objectives: Read accumulated change as the area under a rate graph.
knowledge: The area under a rate-of-change graph is the accumulated change; its units are rate units times input units.

topics.title: Estimating Area with Riemann Sums
objectives: Find left, right, midpoint and trapezoidal sums from graphs, tables or formulas.
knowledge: Subintervals may have equal or unequal widths; tables usually have unequal widths.
For an increasing function a left sum underestimates and a right sum overestimates.

topics.title: Riemann Sums, Sigma Notation and the Definite Integral
objectives: Write a definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums and back.
knowledge: The definite integral is the limit of Riemann sums as the widths shrink to 0.

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem and Accumulation Functions
objectives: Differentiate an accumulation function.
knowledge: The derivative of the integral from a to x of f(t) dt is f(x); with a function as the upper limit, use the chain rule.

topics.title: Behavior of Accumulation Functions
objectives: Analyze an accumulation function from the graph of its integrand.
knowledge: g(x) = integral from a to x of f increases where f > 0 and has extrema where f changes sign.

topics.title: Properties of Definite Integrals
objectives: Use properties of definite integrals and geometry to evaluate integrals.
knowledge: Reversing the limits changes the sign; integrals over adjacent intervals add; areas of triangles and semicircles give exact values.

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem and Definite Integrals
objectives: Evaluate definite integrals with antiderivatives.
knowledge: The integral of f from a to b is F(b) - F(a) when F' = f; the integral of a rate is the net change.

topics.title: Antiderivatives and Indefinite Integrals
objectives: Find antiderivatives with the basic rules and write indefinite integrals with + C.
knowledge: Every derivative rule read backward is an antiderivative rule; some functions have no closed-form antiderivative.

topics.title: Integrating by Substitution
objectives: Integrate by substitution, changing the limits of a definite integral.
knowledge: Choose u so that du appears in the integrand, up to a constant factor.

topics.title: Integrating by Long Division and Completing the Square
objectives: Rewrite an integrand by long division or completing the square before integrating.
knowledge: Completing the square leads to arctangent forms.

topics.title: Choosing an Antidifferentiation Technique
objectives: Choose a technique for an antiderivative.
knowledge: AB scope: basic rules, substitution and rewriting.
exclusions: Integration by parts, partial fractions and improper integrals are BC only (6.11-6.13).

topics.title: Writing Differential Equations
objectives: Write a differential equation from a description.
knowledge: "The rate of change of y is proportional to y" becomes dy/dt = ky.

topics.title: Verifying Solutions to Differential Equations
objectives: Check whether a function solves a differential equation.
knowledge: Differentiate and substitute; a differential equation may have infinitely many solutions.

topics.title: Sketching Slope Fields
objectives: Sketch a slope field at given points.
knowledge: At each point draw a short segment with slope given by the differential equation.

topics.title: Reasoning with Slope Fields
objectives: Sketch a solution curve through a point and reason from a slope field.
knowledge: A solution curve follows the segments; equilibrium solutions are horizontal lines it never crosses.

topics.title: General Solutions by Separation of Variables
objectives: Find the general solution of a separable differential equation.
knowledge: Separate, integrate both sides, add the constant.

topics.title: Particular Solutions from Initial Conditions
objectives: Find a particular solution from an initial condition and state its domain.
knowledge: Use the initial condition as soon as the constant appears; solutions may have a restricted domain.

topics.title: Exponential Models
objectives: Solve and interpret exponential models.
knowledge: dy/dt = ky gives y = y0 times e to the kt.

topics.title: Average Value of a Function
objectives: Find the average value of a function on an interval.
knowledge: Average value = 1/(b - a) times the integral of f from a to b; the integrand is f itself.

topics.title: Motion with Integrals
objectives: Find displacement, total distance and position from velocity.
knowledge: Displacement is the integral of v; total distance is the integral of |v|; position is the starting position plus the integral of v.

topics.title: Accumulation in Context
objectives: Model an amount as a starting value plus the integral of a rate.
knowledge: Amount = initial amount + integral of (rate in - rate out); interpret with units and the interval.

topics.title: Area Between Curves (Functions of x)
objectives: Find the area between curves written as functions of x.
knowledge: Integrate top minus bottom between the intersections.

topics.title: Area Between Curves (Functions of y)
objectives: Find the area between curves written as functions of y.
knowledge: Integrate right minus left with respect to y.

topics.title: Area Between Curves That Cross More Than Twice
objectives: Find the area between curves that intersect at more than two points.
knowledge: Split the integral at each crossing, or integrate the absolute value of the difference.

topics.title: Volumes with Square and Rectangle Cross Sections
objectives: Find volumes with square or rectangular cross sections.
knowledge: Volume is the integral of the cross-section area.

topics.title: Volumes with Triangle and Semicircle Cross Sections
objectives: Find volumes with triangular or semicircular cross sections.
knowledge: Write the area of one cross section from the side length, then integrate.

topics.title: Disc Method About the Axes
objectives: Find volumes of solids of revolution about an axis with discs.
knowledge: Volume = pi times the integral of the radius squared.

topics.title: Disc Method About Other Lines
objectives: Find volumes with discs about a horizontal or vertical line other than an axis.
knowledge: Measure the radius from the axis of rotation.

topics.title: Washer Method About the Axes
objectives: Find volumes with washers about an axis.
knowledge: Volume = pi times the integral of (outer radius squared - inner radius squared).

topics.title: Washer Method About Other Lines
objectives: Find volumes with washers about another horizontal or vertical line.
knowledge: Both radii are distances from the axis of rotation.
exclusions: Arc length (8.13) is BC only; the shell method is not a CED topic.

skillsTopics.title: Functions and Their Graphs
objectives: Read and use function notation, domains, graphs, piecewise functions, composition and lines.
knowledge: A function gives one output for each input in its domain.
Slope is rise over run; point-slope form writes a line through a point.
Piecewise functions use different rules on different intervals.

skillsTopics.title: Exponent Rules and Rewriting Powers
objectives: Rewrite roots and reciprocals as powers and back.
knowledge: A negative exponent is a reciprocal; a fractional exponent is a root.

skillsTopics.title: Algebra for Limits: Factoring and Rationalizing
objectives: Factor, rationalize and simplify complex fractions.
knowledge: Difference of squares and trinomial factoring cancel common factors.
Multiplying by the conjugate rationalizes a numerator or denominator.

skillsTopics.title: Trigonometry and the Unit Circle
objectives: Use radians, the unit circle, the six trigonometric functions and the Pythagorean identity.
knowledge: Calculus measures angles in radians.
The unit circle gives exact sine and cosine values at the special angles.

skillsTopics.title: Exponentials and Logarithms
objectives: Use exponential functions, the natural logarithm and the log rules.
knowledge: ln x and e to the x undo each other.
Log rules turn products into sums and powers into factors.

skillsTopics.title: Inverse Functions
objectives: Find and read inverse functions, including the inverse trigonometric functions.
knowledge: An inverse swaps inputs and outputs; its graph is the reflection in y = x.
arcsin, arccos and arctan have restricted ranges.

skillsTopics.title: Geometry for Calculus
objectives: Use similar triangles, the Pythagorean theorem and area and volume formulas.
knowledge: Similar triangles have proportional sides.
Know the area of a circle, triangle and trapezoid and the volume of a cone, cylinder and sphere.

verified: 1.2 the epsilon-delta definition of a limit
bcOnly: Unit 9 parametric, polar and vector-valued functions
notInCed: indeterminate forms other than 0/0 and infinity/infinity (0 times infinity, 1 to the infinity, infinity minus infinity)
exclusionsSummary.unverifiedUnits3to8: No exclusion statement in Units 3-8 could be read; a person checks the PDF (needs-author units3to8-objectives).

exam.delivery: Hybrid digital in Bluebook: multiple choice on screen; free-response questions read on screen and handwritten in paper booklets.

mcq.format: Single-select only; discrete items and sets that share a graph or a table.

types.table: Rate in context from a table
types.graph: Graph of f′ or graphical FTC
types.fg: Table of f, g, f′ and g′

frq.note: Types recur but are not fixed to a slot; at least two questions are in a real-world context.

exam.calculator: Graphing calculator required in MCQ Part B and FRQ Part A, not allowed in the other parts (Bluebook has Desmos built in). Four required capabilities: graph in a window, find zeros, numerical derivative, numerical definite integral. Show the setup; decimal answers correct to three places (rounded or truncated); radian mode.
exam.previousFormat: 2025 and 2026: MCQ Part A 30 in 60 min, Part B 15 in 45 min; FRQ unchanged.
